gaps.sentence: Little did the suspects ___ that the police were listening.
gaps.explanation: 'Little did they know' — 'know' as bare verb after the inverted auxiliary 'did'.

gaps.sentence: ___ the rain to stop, we'll play the match as planned.
gaps.explanation: Should the rain stop = If the rain stops — should + subject + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: Seldom have I been so ___ by a performance.
gaps.explanation: 'moved' — the audience was emotionally affected; inversion with have been.

gaps.sentence: Barely ___ the ink dried when the complaints began to arrive.
gaps.explanation: 'Barely had the ink dried when …' — inverted past perfect.

gaps.sentence: At no time ___ the crew aware of the danger.
gaps.explanation: 'At no time was the crew aware' — inverted past simple of be.

gaps.sentence: Only by chance ___ the letters discovered decades later.
gaps.explanation: 'Only by chance were the letters discovered' — inverted passive.

gaps.sentence: Not until every passenger had been evacuated ___ the captain leave the ship.
gaps.explanation: 'Not until … did the captain leave …' — inverted past simple.

gaps.sentence: So convinced ___ he of his innocence that he refused the deal.
gaps.explanation: 'So convinced was he of …' — inversion after fronted 'so + adj'.
